title: Electron Capture vs. Transfer Dissociation for Site Determination of Tryptic Peptide Tyrosine Sulfation: Direct Detection of Fibrinogen Sulfation Sites and Identification of Novel Isobaric Interferences
projectDescription: Tyrosine sulfation is an understudied posttranslational modification (PTM) of crucial biological significance. Conventional liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) methods are unable to directly identify sulfation sites due to the high lability of the sulfate PTM. In this study, we were able to directly detect and localize tyrosine sulfation sites in a proteomics workflow. To meet that objective, we combined bottom-up nanoflow LC-beam-type CID (nanoLC-HCD) with conventional “MSFragger-Labile” analysis, nanoLC-electron transfer with supplemental HCD (EThcD) MS/MS, and LC-electron capture dissociation (ECD) MS/MS for the characterization of bovine fibrinogen sulfopeptide candidates from both purified protein and from plasma.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Bovine fibrinogen and bovine plasma were treated with dithiothreitol (DTT) and iodoacetamide (IAA) then digested with trypsin at 1:50 enzyme: protein ratio. Tryptic peptides were then desalted using C18 Spin Columns before LC-MS/MS analysis. Peptide samples were separated on a reverse-phase nanoLC coupled to an orbitrap Fusion or on LC/Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance (FT-ICR) MS analysis. MS analysis was performed by applying high resolution HCD and EThcD on the orbitrap Fusion and ECD on the FT-ICR in data-dependent mode.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw HCD spectra were searched by two different search tools (MSFragger “labile”, and Proteome Discoverer) against UniProt- Bos Tauras sequence database. FDR 1% was applied to MSFragger search results for peptide and protein identification while MS Amanda and Sequest Xcorr scores were used to evaluate peptide identifications in Proteome Discoverer. For LC-ECD MS/MS data annotation, an in- house custom method was developed on Bruker DataAnalysis software (version 5.2) by correlating theoretical ions with experimental data. Theoretical ions masses were exported from Protein Prospector.
